events.title: Stay indoors until lunchtime Friday, government advises
events.summary: The government's 5.30pm update warns that conditions could become more severe. Islanders should remain indoors during the worst of the weather and avoid unnecessary travel or outdoor activity until lunchtime on Friday.
events.details: The weather situation is still developing, with the potential for conditions to become more severe, and the red warning remains in place [1]. Islanders are advised to remain indoors during the worst of the weather and avoid unnecessary travel or outdoor activity until lunchtime on Friday [1][2][3]. Travel disruption, fallen trees and localised flooding are likely. The clean-up will begin on Friday once the red warning has passed and it is safe [1]. The Customer Hub stays open. The Patient Transport Service will run for Friday outpatient appointments, and anyone who no longer needs it should cancel on 444750 [1]. A further update is due on Friday morning [1].

events.title: Heritage sites, the zoo and many shops shut or open late on Friday; fuel paused
events.summary: Jersey Heritage sites and Jersey Zoo are closed on Friday. Co-op, Waitrose and M&S open at 1pm, and Rubis has paused fuel deliveries and forecourts until at least midday.
events.details: All Jersey Heritage sites are closed on Friday, including Jersey Museum, Mont Orgueil and Elizabeth Castle [3][4]. Jersey Zoo is also closed [2]. M&S stores open from 1pm [1], and Co-op food and pharmacy stores in Jersey and Guernsey open at 1pm, so shoppers are asked to buy essentials on Thursday [5]. There are no Jersey Dairy deliveries on Friday [6]. Friday's Field of Remembrance ceremony is postponed, with a reduced service at the Cenotaph on Saturday at 10.30am [1]. Rubis has closed its offices and paused fuel deliveries and forecourts until at least midday on Friday [7]. The Digital Jersey Hub is closed [8]. Waitrose opens at 1pm on Friday and reopens at 8am on Saturday [9].

events.title: Colleges, parks, sports centres, recycling and the Customer Hub shut on Friday
events.summary: The government's 11am update lists the public services closing on Friday, including all schools and colleges, three parks, La Collette and the sports centres. The Union Street Customer Hub, first due to stay open, will now close on Friday morning and reopen at 1pm.
events.details: On Friday, La Collette recycling centre and green waste site will be closed, along with Howard Davis, Coronation (Millbrook) and Sir Winston Churchill parks. Sports centres will stay shut until at least 3pm, and the Jersey and Western libraries will close in the morning [1][2]. All youth clubs are closed on Thursday night, and CAMHS at Bermuda House will be closed on Friday [1]. Highlands College and University College Jersey are also closed on Friday [3]. St Helier's Friday refuse collections move to Saturday 24 October [4]. At 8:57pm the government said the Union Street Customer Hub will now be closed on Friday morning and expects to reopen at 1pm unless otherwise advised [5][6].

events.title: DFDS cancels Jersey–St Malo sailings for the rest of the week and weekend
events.summary: DFDS has cancelled Jersey–St Malo high-speed sailings for the rest of the week and the weekend. An extra return sailing is planned for Monday 26 October.
events.details: DFDS has cancelled Jersey services up to and including Friday and is reviewing Saturday and Sunday sailings between Jersey and St Malo [1]. It has since cancelled Saturday's 07:30 St Malo–Jersey and 09:25 Jersey–St Malo sailings [2], and Sunday's 06:30 St Malo–Jersey and 08:25 Jersey–St Malo sailings [3]. Affected customers will be contacted directly [2][3]. DFDS later cancelled the high-speed Jersey–St Malo service for the rest of the week and the whole weekend. The next sailing is an extra return on Monday 26 October [4][5]. Extra Sunday sailings with Stena Vinga on the Portsmouth route and the freight ship Caesarea Trader are being considered, weather permitting, and DFDS's terminal offices are closed on Friday [4][5].

events.title: All Government of Jersey schools to close on Friday
events.summary: The Education Minister closed all government schools for Friday 23 October a day and a half early, as Jersey Met forecast gusts of 70–80mph.
events.details: The Government of Jersey announced at 6:10pm on Wednesday that all its schools would close on Friday, warning of gusts of 70–80mph, travel disruption, fallen trees and localised flooding [1]. Education Minister Catherine Curtis made the decision early to give families time to arrange childcare; independent schools and private nurseries had not yet confirmed their plans [4]. The government said Storm Austen was not predicted to be as severe as Ciarán or Goretti [3][4], and a red wind warning was expected to be issued early on Thursday [3].
